Threat Scenarios: SECURITY-EXCEPTION-SCOPE-EXPANSION: A wildcard or ambiguous exception disables security enforcement beyond the reviewed target and environment.; SECURITY-EXCEPTION-SELF-APPROVAL: A control owner accepts their own risk without an independent reviewer or accountable approval decision.; SECURITY-EXCEPTION-PERMANENCE: An exception remains effective after its reviewed context and remediation deadline have expired.; SECURITY-EXCEPTION-REGISTER-TAMPERING: An exception is deleted added or modified outside the complete integrity-bound register while enforcement continues.; SECURITY-EXCEPTION-EVIDENCE-LEAK: Approval evidence copies credentials source code production payloads or other sensitive content into a wider audit system.; SECURITY-EXCEPTION-FAIL-OPEN: Missing stale malformed or unavailable exception evidence is interpreted as an approved exception or clean result.
Threat Actor or Source: contributor operator or approver using a broad selector accidentally or to bypass unrelated security decisions
Row Attack or Failure Scenario: one approved case suppresses all scanner findings dependencies repositories builds or environments because its scope is ambiguous
Why This Check Is Required: an exception can be safely evaluated only when the authorized decision and the enforcement target use the same exact identifiers
Required State: every exception names one existing control and check pair plus an exact allowed target type target identifier and environment without wildcard scope
Verification Method: compare exception control_id and check_id with repository metadata and reject wildcard target or environment values
Expected Result: exact existing pairs pass while wildcard unknown and mismatched pairs fail
Required Evidence: normalized exception state without target payload; catalog mismatch negative-test output
Limitations: Repository fixtures do not prove that a production ticket system policy engine or deployment gate enforces the evaluated decision.; SHA-256 detects mismatch against the supplied register but does not prevent an actor with write access from changing both files and hashes so independent immutable approval evidence remains necessary.; Production evaluation requires a trusted UTC time source and must not let exception beneficiaries choose an earlier evaluation time.; The fixed schema prevents payload fields and detects representative credential patterns but cannot recognize every sensitive value hidden inside free text.; Existing control-local exception formats require staged adapters and drift monitoring until migration to the shared interface is complete.; A valid exception documents bounded accepted risk and never changes the underlying failed security condition into PASS.; Passing fixtures do not establish formal NIST SSDF or OpenSSF Baseline compliance.
